name: Bad company (duḥsaṅga)
description: Association with the worldly and faithless, which breeds desire, anger, delusion, loss of memory, loss of understanding and utter ruin; these begin as ripples and become an ocean through association (NBS 43–45).

equivalents.note: the passions it breeds — desire, anger, delusion (cf. BhG 2.62–63; 3.37)

name: Pride and hypocrisy (abhimāna, dambha)
description: The Lord dislikes pride and loves humility (NBS 27); pride, hypocrisy and the like are to be abandoned (NBS 64); pride of learning and birth has no place among devotees (NBS 72).

name: Disputation (vāda)
description: Argument is not to be resorted to, because it gives room for excess and is inconclusive (NBS 74–75).

name: Talk of lust, wealth, unbelievers and enemies
description: Stories of women (as objects of lust), wealth, unbelievers and enemies are not to be listened to (NBS 63).

name: Forgetting the Lord
description: Forgetting the Lord is supreme anguish for the devotee (NBS 19); the Āḻvārs fear that at death, with the throat choked, remembrance will fail, and so entrust that hour to the Lord now (Mukundamālā; PAT 4.10.1).

name: Pride of birth; judging devotees by caste (jāti-abhimāna)
description: Measuring devotees by caste, learning or family: the Āḻvārs teach that the servants of the Lord's servants, even caṇḍālas, are one's masters, and that Veda-learned brāhmaṇas who revile devotees become outcastes; the Nārada Sūtra that no such distinction exists among devotees because they are the Lord's own; the Bhāgavata that a devoted dog-cooker is better than a brāhmaṇa averse to the Lord.

equivalents.note: the Śrīvaiṣṇava offence against devotees includes judging them by birth

name: Reliance on other supports or other gods (anyāśraya)
description: Single-mindedness is the giving up of other supports (NBS 10); the Āḻvārs reproach those who, though the Lord created all, go worshipping other gods (TVM 4.10.1).

name: The five senses as thieves (aivar)
description: The five senses, pictured by the Āḻvārs as a band that plunders the self, to be put under guard by the Lord's name (Tirumālai 1).

name: The sea of births and sorrow (piṟavi, iṭar āḻi)
description: The round of births, pictured as an ocean of sorrow, from which the Āḻvārs ask release at the Lord's feet; the false knowledge, evil conduct and impure body in which the soul has stood (Tiruviruttam 1).

name: The 'śaṭha' wind of forgetting
description: In the hagiographies, the wind (śaṭha-vāyu) that touches every newborn and makes it forget its knowledge; Nammāḻvār repelled it at birth, hence his name Śaṭhakopa ('angry at śaṭha').

name: Love that seeks its own pleasure (the paramour's love)
description: Love without knowledge of the Lord's greatness, and without happiness in his happiness, is like the love of paramours; the gopīs' love had neither fault (NBS 22–24).
